title: The elbow: a hinge joint and an antagonistic pair
caption: A synovial joint has cartilage on the bone ends, synovial fluid and a capsule; ligaments join bone to bone. Muscles are attached to bones by tendons and can only pull. At the elbow, a hinge joint, the biceps and triceps are an antagonistic pair: when the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes the forearm is pulled up; to straighten the arm the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes. The bones act as levers with the joint as the pivot.
alt: A side view of an arm bent at the elbow. The humerus is horizontal and the forearm points up to the right. A capsule round the joint holds synovial fluid, with cartilage on the bone ends and ligaments joining the bones. A thick, contracted biceps above is joined to the forearm by a tendon, and a thin, relaxed triceps below is joined by a tendon behind the elbow.
description: Synovial joint: cartilage, synovial fluid and a capsule; ligaments join bone to bone.
Muscles can only pull, so they work in antagonistic pairs: one contracts while the other relaxes.
Bending the elbow: the biceps contracts and shortens, the triceps relaxes and lengthens, and the forearm is pulled up about the hinge joint.
Bones act as levers, with the joint as the pivot.
